title: Exploring Multi-Player Social Games as Verifiable Training Grounds for Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.31821v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The training of socially intelligent language models often relies on large language model (LLM) judges, which are expensive, noisy, and vulnerable to reward hacking. Multi-player social games offer a natural alternative: they require open-ended communication to coordinate with teammates and infer hidden roles, while their rules provide an objective outcome which can serve as a verifiable reward for training. Using three social games, we explore how much social intelligence Qwen3 models can acquire through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Results show that against a much stronger Gemma-3-27B model, SFT and RLVR raise the win rate of Qwen3-4B from 33% to 81% on the three trained games, and from 39% to 54% on three additional held-out games. translated_title: 探索多人社交游戏作为大语言模型的可验证训练场
translated_abstract: 训练具有社交智能的语言模型通常依赖于大语言模型（LLM）评判者，但这种方式成本高昂、噪声大且容易受到奖励作弊的影响。多人社交游戏提供了一种天然的替代方案：它们需要开放式的沟通来与队友协作并推断隐藏角色，同时其规则提供了客观的胜负结果，可以作为训练中的可验证奖励。本文通过三个社交游戏，探索了Qwen3模型通过监督微调（SFT）和基于可验证奖励的强化学习（RLVR）能够习得多少社交智能。结果表明，面对强大得多的Gemma-3-27B模型，SFT和RLVR将Qwen3-4B在三个训练游戏上的胜率从33%提升至81%，在另外三个未训练的保留游戏上的胜率从39%提升至54%。相比之下，提示等上下文内策略在相同的训练和评估游戏上仅将Qwen3-4B的胜率提高约6个百分点。
tldr: 本文提出将多人社交游戏作为可验证训练环境，通过SFT和RLVR使Qwen3-4B的胜率从33%大幅提升至81%，超越了远大于自身的Gemma-3-27B模型，并能泛化到未见过的游戏中，效果远优于提示等上下文策略。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes multi-player social games as verifiable training grounds, showing that SFT and RLVR boost Qwen3-4B's win rate from 33% to 81%—surpassing the much larger Gemma-3-27B—and generalize to held-out games, far outperforming in-context strategies like prompting.
